correctness.rationale: Write Z=R(cos U,sin U) with R Rayleigh and U uniform modulo pi. For projective gaps d_j the upper survival tail is sum F_t(d_j), with F_t(d)=(2/pi) integral_0^{d/2} exp(-t²/(2sin²u))du and F_t strictly convex. Bisecting maximizes the benefit I_t(d)=F_t(d)-2F_t(d/2), whose derivative is positive, proving the one-addition claim for every t. Squared-moment identity E M²=1-sum_j sin(d_j)/pi, plus sine strict concavity, reduces two additions to gap-subdivision allocations (3,1),(2,2),(1,3). The exact rational sine bounds in frozen verify_completion.py establish that the sine sum at A exceeds that at B by more than 0.028 and at C by more than 0.8, hence E[M_B²]-E[M_A²]>0.028/pi and E[M_C²]-E[M_A²]>0.8/pi; A is the unique squared-moment optimizer. Yet B has smaller largest gap (13π/40 vs 14π/40), so its Laplace exponent makes its upper tail smaller for all sufficiently large thresholds. Any universal optimizer must be A from second moment, contradiction. Independent 35-digit quadrature gave E[M_B²]-E[M_A²]=0.00913238677; B tail below A at t=2,4,6, while t=1 reverses. The analytic comparison, not quadrature, proves all t.
